title: Scope of supply
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Defines supply to include all forms of supply of goods or services made for a consideration in the course or furtherance of business, and activities specified in Schedule I even without consideration. Schedule III activities are neither supply of goods nor services.

title: Permanent transfer or disposal of business assets
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Permanent transfer or disposal of business assets on which input tax credit has been availed is treated as supply even if made without consideration.

title: Supply between related persons or distinct persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Supply of goods or services between related persons, or between distinct persons as specified in Section 25, when made in the course or furtherance of business, is treated as supply even without consideration. Gifts by an employer to an employee not exceeding Rs 50,000 in a financial year are excluded.

title: Import of services from related person without consideration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Import of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of its other establishments outside India, in the course or furtherance of business, is a supply even without consideration.

title: Supply of warehoused goods before clearance for home consumption
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Supply of warehoused goods to any person before clearance for home consumption is treated as neither a supply of goods nor a supply of services. The paragraph was inserted by the CGST (Amendment) Act, 2018 and its retrospective application was subsequently provided by a later Finance Act.

title: Levy and collection of CGST
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: CGST is levied on intra-State supplies of goods or services at rates notified on the recommendation of the GST Council, on the value determined under Section 15.

title: Reverse charge on notified supplies
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The Government may notify categories of supply of goods or services on which tax is payable by the recipient on reverse charge basis, with all provisions applying to the recipient as if it were the person liable to pay tax.

title: Reverse charge on supplies from unregistered persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Tax on notified categories of supply by an unregistered supplier to a notified class of registered persons is payable by the recipient on reverse charge basis (currently limited to notified classes such as specified real estate promoters).

title: Tax payable by electronic commerce operator
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: For notified categories of services supplied through an electronic commerce operator (such as specified passenger transport, accommodation, housekeeping and restaurant services), the ECO is liable to pay the tax as if it were the supplier.

title: Composition levy
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Permits eligible taxpayers below the notified turnover limit to pay tax at a concessional rate on turnover. A composition taxpayer cannot collect tax from recipients nor is it entitled to input tax credit, and must issue a bill of supply.

title: Time of supply of goods
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Time of supply of goods is the earlier of the date of issue of invoice (or last date by which it should have been issued) and date of receipt of payment; tax on advances for goods has been exempted by notification for taxpayers other than composition taxpayers.

title: Time of supply of goods under reverse charge
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: For goods taxable under reverse charge, time of supply is the earliest of date of receipt of goods, date of payment, or the date immediately following thirty days from the date of supplier's invoice.

title: Time of supply of services
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Time of supply of services is generally the earlier of the date of invoice (if issued within the prescribed period) and date of receipt of payment, with specific rules for reverse charge and associated enterprises.

title: Time of supply of services under reverse charge
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: For services taxable under reverse charge, time of supply is the earlier of the date of payment and the date immediately following sixty days from the supplier's invoice; for associated enterprises located outside India, it is the earlier of date of entry in the books of the recipient and date of payment.

title: Value of taxable supply
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Value of supply is the transaction value where supplier and recipient are not related and price is the sole consideration; otherwise value is determined under the valuation rules.

title: Inclusions in value of supply
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Value includes taxes other than GST charged separately, amounts the supplier is liable to pay but incurred by the recipient, incidental expenses such as commission and packing, interest/late fee/penalty for delayed payment, and subsidies directly linked to price (excluding Government subsidies).

title: Discounts excluded from value of supply
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Discount given before or at the time of supply and recorded in the invoice is excluded from value. Post-supply discount is excluded only if established by an agreement entered into before or at the time of supply, specifically linked to relevant invoices, and the recipient has reversed the attributable input tax credit.

title: Eligibility for input tax credit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: A registered person is entitled to credit of input tax charged on supply of goods or services used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of business, subject to prescribed conditions and restrictions.

title: Conditions for availing input tax credit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: ITC is available only if the recipient holds a tax invoice/debit note, the details are furnished by the supplier and communicated (clause (aa)), goods or services have been received (including bill-to-ship-to), tax has been actually paid to the Government by the supplier, and the recipient has furnished its return. Credit is to be reversed if the supplier is not paid within 180 days.

title: ITC restricted to details communicated in GSTR-2B
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Inserted with effect from 01.01.2022, ITC is available only where the supplier has furnished the invoice/debit note in its outward statement and such details are communicated to the recipient (GSTR-2B).

title: No ITC on tax component claimed as depreciation
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where depreciation has been claimed under the Income-tax Act on the tax component of the cost of capital goods and plant and machinery, ITC on that tax component is not allowed.

title: Time limit for availing input tax credit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: ITC in respect of an invoice or debit note cannot be availed after the thirtieth day of November following the end of the financial year to which it pertains, or the date of furnishing the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier. The 30 November cut-off applies as amended with effect from 01.10.2022 (earlier: due date of September return).

title: Extended time limit for FY 2017-18 to 2020-21
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Inserted by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 with retrospective effect, permits ITC for FY 2017-18 to FY 2020-21 availed in any return filed up to 30 November 2021, notwithstanding Section 16(4).

title: Apportionment of credit for business and exempt use
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where goods or services are used partly for business and partly for other purposes, or partly for taxable and partly for exempt supplies (including non-taxable supplies), credit is restricted to the portion attributable to business and taxable/zero-rated supplies, computed under Rules 42 and 43.

title: Blocked input tax credit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Lists credits not available, including motor vehicles and conveyances (with exceptions), food and beverages, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, life and health insurance, club membership, travel benefits to employees (unless obligatory under law), works contract and construction of immovable property (other than plant and machinery), goods lost/stolen/destroyed/written off or disposed by way of gift or free samples, and tax paid under Sections 74, 129 and 130.

title: ITC on new registration and changes in scheme
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Provides credit on stock held on the day preceding the date of becoming liable to register or obtaining registration, subject to conditions and a one-year time limit from the invoice date.

title: Transfer of ITC on change in constitution or business transfer
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where there is a change in constitution of a registered person on account of sale, merger, demerger, amalgamation, lease or transfer of business with specific provision for transfer of liabilities, the unutilised ITC may be transferred to the transferee in the prescribed manner (Form GST ITC-02).

title: Supply of capital goods on which ITC has been taken
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: On supply of capital goods or plant and machinery on which ITC has been taken, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the ITC taken reduced by the prescribed percentage points, or the tax on transaction value, whichever is higher. Refractory bricks, moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures supplied as scrap may pay tax on transaction value.

title: ITC on inputs and capital goods sent for job work
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Principal may avail ITC on inputs and capital goods sent to a job worker; if inputs are not received back within one year, or capital goods within three years (other than moulds, dies, jigs, fixtures and tools), they are deemed supplied on the day they were sent out.

title: Manner of distribution of credit by Input Service Distributor
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: As substituted with effect from 01.04.2025, any office receiving invoices for input services, including services subject to reverse charge, for or on behalf of distinct persons is required to register as an ISD and distribute such credit in the prescribed manner.

title: Persons liable for registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every supplier whose aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds the threshold (Rs 20 lakh / Rs 10 lakh for special category States; Rs 40 lakh for exclusive goods suppliers in States that have adopted it) is liable to register in each State/UT from which taxable supply is made.

title: Compulsory registration in certain cases
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Specified persons must register irrespective of turnover, including inter-State taxable suppliers (subject to exemptions), persons liable under reverse charge, ECOs, TDS deductors, ISDs, and non-resident taxable persons.

title: Procedure for registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Registration is required in every State/UT where the person is liable, within 30 days; separate registrations may be obtained for each place of business. Establishments with separate registrations are treated as distinct persons (Section 25(4)).

title: Distinct persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: A person who has obtained or is required to obtain more than one registration, in one or more States, is treated as a distinct person in respect of each such registration.

title: Amendment of registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every registered person shall inform the proper officer of any change in the information furnished at the time of registration, including addition of places of business, within the prescribed period (Rule 19: 15 days).

title: Cancellation or suspension of registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Provides for cancellation of registration on application or by the proper officer for non-compliance, including non-filing of returns, and for suspension pending proceedings.

title: Tax invoice
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: A registered person supplying goods or services must issue a tax invoice within the prescribed time containing prescribed particulars; separate provisions govern bills of supply, receipt vouchers, refund vouchers and payment vouchers.

title: Self-invoice and payment voucher for reverse charge
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: A registered person liable to pay tax under Section 9(3) or 9(4) on supplies from an unregistered supplier must issue an invoice in respect of such goods or services, and a payment voucher at the time of making payment to the supplier.

title: Credit and debit notes
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Credit notes may be issued where taxable value or tax in an invoice exceeds the actual value, goods are returned, or services are found deficient. Details of a credit note must be declared not later than 30 November following the end of the financial year of the supply or the date of furnishing the annual return, whichever is earlier, and output tax reduction is not permitted if the incidence has been passed on.

title: Accounts and other records
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every registered person shall keep and maintain at the principal place of business true and correct accounts of production, inward and outward supplies, stock, ITC availed, output tax payable and paid, and other prescribed particulars, for each place of business.

title: Period of retention of accounts
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Accounts and records shall be retained until the expiry of 72 months from the due date of furnishing the annual return for the year to which they pertain; longer if subject to appeal, revision, or other proceedings.

title: Furnishing details of outward supplies (GSTR-1)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every registered person shall furnish details of outward supplies in the prescribed form (GSTR-1) for each tax period; details cannot be furnished after the expiry of three years from the due date, and are subject to prescribed restrictions.

title: Furnishing of returns (GSTR-3B)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every registered person shall furnish a return for each tax period with details of inward and outward supplies, ITC availed, tax payable and tax paid, and shall pay the tax due not later than the last date for furnishing the return.

title: Annual return
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every registered person (other than notified exceptions) shall furnish an annual return for each financial year, with a self-certified reconciliation statement for notified classes, by 31 December following the end of the financial year.

title: Levy of late fee
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Late fee is payable for delayed furnishing of returns including GSTR-1, GSTR-3B and the annual return, at rates and subject to caps as notified by the Government.

title: Payment of tax, interest, penalty and other amounts
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Payments are credited to the electronic cash ledger and ITC to the electronic credit ledger; credit may be used only for output tax. Reverse-charge tax, interest, penalty and late fee are payable through the cash ledger. Balance in the cash ledger may be refunded under Section 54.

title: Utilisation of input tax credit subject to certain conditions
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: IGST credit must be fully utilised towards IGST, CGST and SGST liability before CGST or SGST credit is utilised; read with Rule 88A on the order of utilisation.

title: Interest on delayed payment of tax
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Interest at the notified rate (18% p.a.) is payable on tax not paid within the due period; interest on delayed payment of tax declared in a return filed after the due date is levied on the portion paid by debiting the electronic cash ledger, except where the return is filed after commencement of proceedings under Sections 73/74.

title: Interest on ITC wrongly availed and utilised
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Interest at the notified rate (18% p.a.) is payable where ITC has been wrongly availed and utilised, computed in the prescribed manner (Rule 88B). Mere availment without utilisation does not attract interest. The substituted provision applies retrospectively from 01.07.2017.

title: Tax deduction at source
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Notified Government departments, local authorities, agencies and other notified persons deduct TDS at 2% (1% CGST + 1% SGST, or 2% IGST) on payments to suppliers of taxable goods or services where the contract value exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh, and file GSTR-7; the deductee may claim the credit in its electronic cash ledger.

title: Collection of tax at source by e-commerce operator
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Every electronic commerce operator not being an agent shall collect tax at the notified rate on the net value of taxable supplies made through it by other suppliers where consideration is collected by the operator, and furnish GSTR-8; suppliers claim the amount in their electronic cash ledger.

title: Refund of tax
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Refund of tax, interest or other amounts may be claimed within two years from the relevant date; refund of unutilised ITC is permitted for zero-rated supplies without payment of tax and for inverted duty structure, subject to conditions. Balance in electronic cash ledger may be refunded as prescribed.

title: Scrutiny of returns
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The proper officer may scrutinise returns and inform discrepancies (Form ASMT-10) seeking explanation; if the explanation is accepted no further action is taken, otherwise action may be initiated including audit, special audit, or demand proceedings.

title: Audit by tax authorities
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The Commissioner may undertake audit of a registered person with prior notice (Form ADT-01); audit is to be completed within three months (extendable by six months), and findings are communicated in Form ADT-02.

title: Determination of tax not paid or ITC wrongly availed (non-fraud)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Governs demands for tax not paid, short paid, erroneously refunded or ITC wrongly availed or utilised for reasons other than fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression, for periods up to FY 2023-24. Order must be issued within three years from the due date of the annual return; no penalty if tax and interest are paid before notice, and reduced exposure if paid within 30 days of notice.

title: Determination of tax not paid or ITC wrongly availed (fraud/suppression)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Governs demands involving fraud, wilful misstatement or suppression of facts for periods up to FY 2023-24, with an extended limitation of five years from the due date of the annual return and penalty equal to the tax (reduced if paid at earlier stages). ITC on tax paid under Section 74 is blocked by Section 17(5).

title: Determination of tax for FY 2024-25 onwards
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Inserted by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024, provides a common procedure for demands relating to FY 2024-25 onwards, both fraud and non-fraud. Notice is to be issued within 42 months from the due date of annual return (or date of erroneous refund) and the order within 12 months of notice, extendable; penalty differs for fraud and non-fraud cases.

title: General provisions relating to determination of tax
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Lays down procedural safeguards in demand proceedings including opportunity of personal hearing where requested or adverse decision contemplated, a maximum of three adjournments, and that demand cannot exceed the amount specified in the notice or be confirmed on grounds not in the notice.

title: Tax wrongfully collected and paid to Central/State Government
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where a person has paid CGST/SGST on a transaction considered intra-State that is subsequently held to be inter-State (or vice versa), the tax paid under the wrong head is refunded and the person is not required to pay interest on the amount payable under the correct head.

title: Appeals to Appellate Authority
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Appeal against an order may be filed within three months from communication (condonable by one further month), subject to mandatory pre-deposit of admitted tax and 10% of the disputed tax subject to the statutory monetary cap; filing with pre-deposit stays recovery of the balance.

title: Penalty for certain offences
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes penalties for specified offences, including supply without invoice or with incorrect invoice, issuing invoice without supply, failing to deduct or collect tax, availing ITC without receipt of goods or services, and transporting goods without prescribed documents.

title: General penalty
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Any contravention for which no separate penalty is provided is liable to a penalty which may extend to Rs 25,000.

title: Waiver of interest or penalty for FY 2017-18 to 2019-20
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Inserted by the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024, provides for waiver of interest and penalty on demands raised under Section 73 for FY 2017-18 to 2019-20 where the full tax demanded is paid by the notified date, subject to conditions and exclusions (e.g., erroneous refunds). Not applicable to Section 74 demands.

title: Detention, seizure and release of goods in transit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Goods transported in contravention of the Act (including without valid e-way bill) may be detained; release is on payment of penalty (for taxable goods, 200% of the tax payable where the owner comes forward, as amended with effect from 01.01.2022). Tax paid under Section 129 is blocked from ITC.

title: Job work procedure
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: A principal may send inputs and capital goods to a job worker without payment of tax under intimation; inputs must be returned within one year and capital goods within three years, failing which they are deemed supplied from the date of dispatch. Waste and scrap may be supplied by the job worker or principal.

title: Deemed exports
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The Government may notify supplies of goods as deemed exports where goods supplied do not leave India and payment is received in Indian rupees or convertible foreign exchange.

title: Burden of proof
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where a person claims eligibility for input tax credit, the burden of proving such claim lies on that person.

title: Amendment of registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Changes in particulars furnished in the registration application, including addition, deletion or change of places of business, are to be applied for in Form GST REG-14 within 15 days of the change.

title: Suspension of registration
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Registration may be suspended pending cancellation proceedings, including where significant differences are found between GSTR-1/GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B; a suspended person cannot make taxable supplies or claim refunds during suspension.

title: Value of supply between distinct or related persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Value is the open market value, failing which the value of like kind and quality, failing which cost plus 10% or residual method. Where the recipient is eligible for full ITC, the value declared in the invoice is deemed to be the open market value.

title: Value of supply of services as pure agent
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Expenditure incurred as a pure agent of the recipient is excluded from value only where the supplier acts as pure agent under a contract, the recipient receives and is liable to pay for the supply, the expense is separately indicated in the invoice, and the amount recovered is the actual amount paid.

title: Documentary requirements for claiming ITC
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: ITC may be availed on the basis of tax invoice, debit note, invoice for reverse charge, ISD invoice, or bill of entry or similar document prescribed under the Customs Act for assessment of IGST on imports.

title: ITC restricted to invoices reflected in GSTR-2B
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Introduced with effect from 09.10.2019 with a provisional cushion, and amended with effect from 01.01.2022 to restrict ITC on invoices and debit notes to those reported by suppliers and communicated in GSTR-2B.

title: Reversal of ITC on non-payment within 180 days
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Where the recipient fails to pay the supplier the value of supply plus tax within 180 days from the invoice date, the proportionate ITC must be reversed in the return for the period following the 180th day; credit may be re-availed upon payment.

title: Reversal of ITC where supplier has not paid tax
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Where ITC has been availed on invoices reported by the supplier in GSTR-1 but the supplier has not furnished GSTR-3B for the period by 30 September following the end of the financial year, the recipient must reverse the ITC by 30 November; it may be re-availed once the supplier files the return.

title: Procedure for distribution of ITC by ISD
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: ISD credit must be distributed in the same month through an ISD invoice to recipients to whom the input services are attributable, and common credit is distributed pro rata on turnover of the recipients in the relevant State; GSTR-6 is filed monthly.

title: Transfer of credit on sale, merger, amalgamation, lease or transfer of business
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: The transferor files Form GST ITC-02 with a certificate from a practising chartered/cost accountant where there is a specific provision for transfer of liabilities; the transferee accepts the credit on the portal, and inputs and capital goods must be duly accounted in the transferee's books.

title: ITC reversal for inputs and input services used for exempt/non-business purposes
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Prescribes the manner of determining and reversing ITC attributable to exempt supplies and non-business use, on a monthly provisional basis and final computation for the financial year by the due date of the September return following the year end, with interest on short reversal.

title: ITC reversal on capital goods used for exempt/non-business purposes
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Common credit on capital goods is credited to the electronic credit ledger and attributed to exempt supplies over a useful life of five years (60 months) on a monthly basis in the ratio of exempt turnover to total turnover.

title: Amount payable on supply of capital goods
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: For the purpose of Section 18(6), ITC involved in the remaining useful life of capital goods is computed by reducing ITC taken by five percentage points for every quarter or part thereof from the date of invoice.

title: Conditions and restrictions in respect of inputs and capital goods sent to job worker
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Inputs, semi-finished goods or capital goods are sent to the job worker under a challan; details of challans and goods returned are reported in Form GST ITC-04 at the prescribed frequency.

title: Tax invoice
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Prescribes particulars of a tax invoice including consecutive serial number unique for a financial year, GSTIN of recipient, HSN/SAC, taxable value, rate and amount of tax, place of supply, and whether tax is payable on reverse charge.

title: Time limit for issuing tax invoice for services
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Invoice for taxable services shall be issued within 30 days from the date of supply (45 days for banking/insurance and certain financial institutions).

title: Electronic invoicing (IRN)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Notified classes of registered persons must prepare invoices and credit/debit notes for B2B supplies and exports by uploading them to the Invoice Registration Portal to obtain an IRN. An invoice issued otherwise than in this manner is not treated as an invoice (Rule 48(5)).

title: Revised tax invoice and credit or debit notes
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Prescribes the particulars of revised invoices and credit/debit notes, including the serial number and date of the corresponding tax invoice.

title: Transportation of goods without issue of invoice
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: A delivery challan may be issued for movement of goods for job work, supply of liquid gas where quantity is unknown, transportation for reasons other than supply, and other notified cases.

title: Maintenance of accounts by registered persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Specifies the accounts to be maintained, including stock of goods, ITC, output tax, advances, and records at each place of business; electronic records must be backed up and authenticated.

title: Form and manner of furnishing details of outward supplies
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Prescribes GSTR-1 and the Invoice Furnishing Facility; sub-rule (6) restricts furnishing GSTR-1 where GSTR-3B of earlier periods has not been furnished or where Rule 86B conditions are not met.

title: Annual return
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Annual return in Form GSTR-9 is to be furnished by 31 December following the end of the financial year; registered persons above the notified turnover threshold also furnish a self-certified reconciliation statement in Form GSTR-9C.

title: Electronic liability register
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: The electronic liability register records all tax, interest, late fee and penalty liabilities of a registered person, discharged by debiting the electronic cash or credit ledger.

title: Electronic credit ledger
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: ITC as self-assessed in the return is credited to the electronic credit ledger and debited on utilisation or refund; the ledger cannot be in negative balance.

title: Conditions of use of amount available in electronic credit ledger
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: The Commissioner or authorised officer may disallow debit of credit fraudulently availed or ineligible on specified grounds (e.g., non-existent supplier, goods not received, supplier not having paid tax) for up to one year.

title: Restriction on use of ITC to discharge output liability
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Registered persons with monthly taxable supply value exceeding Rs 50 lakh shall discharge at least 1% of output tax liability in cash, subject to specified exceptions (e.g., income-tax above threshold, refunds, cash payments above 1% cumulatively).

title: Electronic cash ledger
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Deposits made through challan (PMT-06) are credited to the electronic cash ledger under major and minor heads. Amounts may be transferred between heads and to distinct persons using Form GST PMT-09, and excess balance may be claimed as refund.

title: Order of utilisation of input tax credit
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: IGST credit shall first be utilised for IGST, and the balance for CGST and SGST in any order, before CGST or SGST credit is utilised; CGST credit cannot be used for SGST and vice versa.

title: Manner of calculating interest on delayed payment of tax and wrongly availed ITC
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Interest under Section 50(3) on wrongly availed ITC is computed on the amount utilised, from the date of utilisation till reversal/payment; utilisation is deemed when the electronic credit ledger balance falls below the wrongly availed amount.

title: Intimation of difference between liability in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Where output tax in GSTR-1 exceeds that paid in GSTR-3B beyond the prescribed limit, the taxpayer receives an intimation in Form DRC-01B and must pay the difference or explain it; non-response blocks furnishing of the next GSTR-1.

title: Intimation of difference between ITC in GSTR-3B and GSTR-2B
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Where ITC availed in GSTR-3B exceeds ITC available in GSTR-2B beyond the prescribed limit, the taxpayer receives an intimation in Form DRC-01C and must reverse the excess or explain it; non-response blocks furnishing of GSTR-1.

title: Application for refund
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Refund is claimed in Form RFD-01 with prescribed documents, including SEZ endorsement for supplies to SEZ, statements of invoices, and the formula in sub-rule (4) for refund of ITC on zero-rated supplies without payment of tax and sub-rule (5) for inverted duty structure.

title: Refund of IGST paid on goods exported
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: The shipping bill filed by an exporter is deemed to be the refund application for IGST paid on export of goods once the export general manifest is filed and a valid GSTR-3B is furnished; GSTR-1 Table 6A details are transmitted to ICEGATE for validation against the shipping bill.

title: Export of goods or services under bond or Letter of Undertaking
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: A registered person may export or supply to SEZ without payment of IGST under a bond or LUT (Form GST RFD-11), undertaking to pay tax with interest if goods are not exported within three months of the invoice date (or extended period), or if payment for services is not received in convertible foreign exchange or INR as permitted by RBI within one year (or extended period).

title: E-way bill
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: An e-way bill must be generated before movement of goods of consignment value exceeding Rs 50,000 (subject to exemptions in sub-rule (14) and State-specific thresholds for intra-State movement), with Part B containing vehicle details; validity is based on distance and may be extended, and an e-way bill may be cancelled within 24 hours if goods are not transported.

title: Documents and devices to be carried by person-in-charge of conveyance
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: The person in charge of a conveyance must carry the invoice, bill of supply or delivery challan and a copy of the e-way bill (physical or mapped to RFID); an IRN may be produced in lieu of the invoice for e-invoiced documents.

title: Notice and order for demand; voluntary payment
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: Prescribes pre-SCN intimation (DRC-01A), show cause notice summary (DRC-01), voluntary payment of tax, interest and penalty (DRC-03), reply (DRC-06) and order summary (DRC-07).

title: Export of services
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Supply of service is export where the supplier is in India, the recipient is outside India, the place of supply is outside India, payment is received in convertible foreign exchange or in INR wherever permitted by RBI, and supplier and recipient are not merely establishments of a distinct person.

title: Import of services
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Supply of service is import where the supplier is located outside India, the recipient is located in India and the place of supply is in India.

title: Reverse charge on notified inter-State supplies
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: IGST on notified categories of supply of goods or services is payable by the recipient on reverse charge basis; import of services by a person in the taxable territory is notified under this provision.

title: Inter-State supply including supply to SEZ
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Supply of goods or services when the supplier is in India and place of supply is outside India, supply to or by a SEZ developer or SEZ unit, and other specified supplies are treated as inter-State supplies.

title: Place of supply of goods (other than imports/exports)
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Place of supply is where movement of goods terminates for delivery; in bill-to-ship-to transactions it is the principal place of business of the person on whose direction goods are delivered.

title: Place of supply of services where supplier and recipient are in India
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Generally the location of a registered recipient; specific rules apply for immovable property, restaurant, training, events, transportation, telecom, banking and other services.

title: Place of supply of services where supplier or recipient is outside India
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Default place of supply is the location of the recipient, with exceptions for performance-based services on goods, immovable property, events, intermediary services (location of supplier), and specified other services.

title: Zero-rated supply
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Export of goods or services and supplies to SEZ developers or units for authorised operations are zero-rated; ITC is available and refund may be claimed either by supplying under bond/LUT without payment of IGST or by paying IGST and claiming refund, subject to conditions.

title: Tax wrongfully collected and paid to Central or State Government
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Where IGST has been paid on a supply subsequently held to be intra-State, the IGST paid is refunded and no interest is payable on CGST/SGST due under the correct head.

title: Valuation of goods
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Value of imported and export goods is the transaction value, including specified costs, where buyer and seller are not related or relationship has not influenced the price, read with the Customs Valuation Rules.

title: Assessment of duty
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Importers and exporters self-assess duty; the proper officer may verify and re-assess, and must pass a speaking order where re-assessment is contrary to the self-assessment and not accepted by the importer.

title: Provisional assessment of duty
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Duty may be provisionally assessed against security where documents or tests are pending; on finalisation, differential duty is payable with interest or refund is granted.

title: Claim for refund of duty
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Refund of duty or interest is claimed within one year from the date of payment or relevant date, subject to unjust enrichment; the limitation does not apply where duty has been paid under protest.

title: Recovery of duties not levied, short-levied or erroneously refunded
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Demand of duty not levied or short-levied may be raised within two years (five years in cases of collusion, wilful misstatement or suppression) from the relevant date.

title: Interest on delayed payment of duty
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Interest at the notified rate is payable on duty not paid or short-paid, in addition to the duty, from the date it was payable until payment.

title: Entry of goods on importation (Bill of Entry)
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Importer shall present a bill of entry for home consumption or warehousing electronically on ICEGATE within the prescribed time, declaring truthful contents and supported by invoices.

title: Entry of goods for exportation (Shipping Bill)
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Exporter shall present a shipping bill electronically on ICEGATE making truthful declarations and ensuring accuracy and completeness of information.

title: Manufacture and other operations in warehouse
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: Permits manufacturing and other operations in a customs bonded warehouse with permission, with import duty deferred on inputs and capital goods (MOOWR scheme); duty is payable on clearance for home consumption, while export clearances are duty-free.

title: Amendment of documents
statute: Customs Act, 1962
summary: The proper officer may permit amendment of a bill of entry or shipping bill after presentation; amendment after clearance or export is permissible only on documentary evidence existing at the time of import/export.

title: IGST on imported goods
statute: Customs Tariff Act, 1975
summary: Imported goods are liable to integrated tax at the rate leviable under the IGST Act on like goods, on the value including assessable value and customs duties (excluding IGST and compensation cess); this IGST is creditable as ITC on the basis of the bill of entry.

title: CGST rates on goods
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes CGST rates on goods by HSN in schedules, as amended from time to time; read with corresponding SGST and IGST rate notifications.

title: Reverse charge on notified goods
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Notifies goods on which tax is payable by the recipient under Section 9(3), such as specified cashew nuts, tendu leaves, tobacco leaves, silk yarn, and certain supplies by specified persons, as amended.

title: CGST rates on services
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes CGST rates on services by heading, including works contract, job work, GTA and other services, as amended from time to time.

title: Exemption of specified services
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Exempts specified services from CGST, including services by way of transfer of a going concern as a whole or an independent part thereof, as amended.

title: Reverse charge on notified services
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Notifies services on which tax is payable by the recipient under Section 9(3), including GTA (where forward charge not opted), legal services by advocates, sponsorship, services by directors to the company, security services by non-body corporates, renting of motor vehicles in specified cases, and (from 10.10.2024) renting of commercial property by an unregistered person to a registered person, as amended.

title: IGST reverse charge on notified services including import of services
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Notifies inter-State services taxable under reverse charge under Section 5(3) of the IGST Act, including services supplied by a person located in a non-taxable territory to a person in the taxable territory (other than non-taxable online recipients), as amended.

title: Concessional rate for supplies to merchant exporters
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes a concessional CGST rate on intra-State supply of goods to registered merchant exporters, subject to conditions including export within 90 days, registration with an export promotion council, and movement directly to port or registered warehouse.

title: Deemed exports
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Notifies supplies treated as deemed exports under Section 147, including supply against Advance Authorisation, supply of capital goods against EPCG authorisation, supply to EOUs, and supply of gold by banks against Advance Authorisation; refund may be claimed by recipient or supplier subject to conditions.

title: E-invoicing applicability threshold
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Rules, 2017
summary: E-invoicing under Rule 48(4) applies to registered persons whose aggregate turnover in any financial year from 2017-18 onwards exceeds the notified threshold, progressively reduced from Rs 500 crore (01.10.2020) to Rs 5 crore (01.08.2023), with specified exempt classes such as SEZ units, insurers, banking companies, GTA and passenger transport service providers.

title: Treatment of sales promotion schemes
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies that free samples and gifts without consideration are not supply (except where covered by Schedule I) and ITC on them is blocked under Section 17(5)(h); in buy-one-get-one offers the free item is part of a composite or mixed supply and ITC is available; discounts in the invoice and pre-agreed volume discounts are excluded from value.

title: Reporting of ITC availed, reversed and ineligible in GSTR-3B
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies reporting in GSTR-3B Table 4: ITC per GSTR-2B to be reported in 4(A), permanent reversals (Rule 38, 42, 43, Section 17(5)) in 4(B)(1), temporary reversals (Rule 37, 37A, Section 16(2)(b)/(c)) in 4(B)(2) with re-claim in 4(A)(5) and 4(D)(1); and reporting of inter-State supplies to unregistered persons in Table 3.2.

title: Clarification on miscellaneous issues including perquisites and Section 17(5)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies, inter alia, that perquisites provided by employer to employee under the contract of employment are not supply, and that the proviso to Section 17(5)(b) (credit allowed where obligatory under any law) applies to the whole of clause (b).

title: Mismatch between ITC in GSTR-3B and GSTR-2A for FY 2017-18 and 2018-19
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes the procedure for verifying ITC claims for FY 2017-18 and 2018-19 where invoices are not reflected in GSTR-2A, including CA/CMA certificates (above a threshold) or supplier certificates confirming supply and payment of tax.

title: Replacement of parts and repair services under warranty
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies that replacement of parts or repair services by the manufacturer without consideration during the warranty period is not taxable and no ITC reversal is required by the manufacturer; it also addresses distributor replacements and extended warranties.

title: Taxability of services between distinct persons and ISD
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies that for common input services procured from third parties, HO may distribute credit through ISD or cross-charge; where the recipient branch is eligible for full ITC, the value declared in the invoice is deemed open market value (including nil), and salary cost of HO employees need not be included in cross-charge value.

title: Valuation of import of services from related persons
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies that where a foreign related person supplies services to an Indian related person eligible for full ITC, the value declared in the invoice may be deemed open market value, and where no invoice is issued the value may be deemed nil, under the second proviso to Rule 28(1).

title: Time limit under Section 16(4) for reverse charge supplies
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Clarifies that for supplies from unregistered persons under reverse charge, the financial year relevant for the Section 16(4) time limit is the year in which the recipient issues the self-invoice under Section 31(3)(f), while noting that delayed self-invoicing attracts interest and penalty.

title: Compliance with Section 15(3)(b)(ii) for post-supply discounts
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: Prescribes the mechanism for suppliers to establish that recipients have reversed ITC attributable to post-supply discounts: certificate from the recipient (or CA/CMA certificate above a threshold) confirming reversal, in addition to the general route of verifying credit note acceptance on the portal.

title: Invoice Management System (IMS)
statute: GST Network portal advisory
summary: IMS allows recipients to accept, reject or keep pending invoices and other records uploaded by suppliers before generation of GSTR-2B, starting with records for the October 2024 tax period; rejected records do not flow to GSTR-2B and accepted/deemed-accepted records do.

title: Time limit for reporting e-invoices on IRP
statute: GST Network portal advisory
summary: GSTN advisories restrict generation of IRN for invoices and credit/debit notes older than 30 days from the date of reporting for notified classes of taxpayers by AATO (initially Rs 100 crore and above from 01.11.2023, later extended to Rs 10 crore and above).

title: Transmission of GSTR-1 Table 6A to ICEGATE for IGST refund
statute: GST Network portal advisory
summary: Export invoice details furnished in GSTR-1 Table 6A, with shipping bill number, date and port code, are transmitted to ICEGATE and validated against the shipping bill and EGM; mismatches result in error responses that block the automated IGST refund until corrected (including through Table 9A amendments or officer intervention).

title: Chief Commissioner of CGST v. Safari Retreats Pvt Ltd (Supreme Court, 2024)
statute: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The Supreme Court held that whether a building is a 'plant or machinery' under Section 17(5)(d) is a functionality test to be applied on facts. Parliament subsequently amended Section 17(5)(d) retrospectively to read 'plant and machinery'; the position must be evaluated with the amended provision.

title: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd (Supreme Court, 2022)
provision: IGST reverse charge on ocean freight
statute: Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017
summary: The Supreme Court held that levy of IGST under reverse charge on ocean freight for CIF imports, where the importer is not the recipient of the transport service and IGST is already paid on the CIF value of goods, is unsustainable as a composite supply already taxed.

title: CCE v. Northern Operating Systems Pvt Ltd (Supreme Court, 2022)
provision: Secondment of employees by overseas group entity
statute: Finance Act, 1994 (service tax); principles applied in GST
summary: The Supreme Court held that secondment of employees by an overseas group company to the Indian entity, with salary cost reimbursed, constituted supply of manpower service by the overseas entity taxable in the hands of the Indian recipient under reverse charge, depending on the facts of the arrangement.
